reviews.title: Good quality (universal) desk boom for the money
reviews.comment:
Time spent with item: 48 hours
Note: I am an audio visual producer of more than ten years, so I have extensive experience with audio equipment of all kinds. I have, also, instrumental experience of over twenty years.
Disclaimer: I used this clamping boom stand with the 512 Audio Skylight Studio Condenser mic using the included threaded adapter. It is the heaviest microphone I have on hand in my home. I have another clamping boom stand as well and a fixed boom stand, in addition.
Pros:
* it seemed to hold where I put it without drooping under the mics weight
* it is SMALL. The unit measures about a foot long per arm so about two feet total.
* it seemed fairly sturdy for the price
* it didn’t make too much noise when adjusting, I am using a shock mount though
* it gave me as much range of motion (adjustability) as my $80 clamping boom mic stand.
* can be used with any style of mic under the weight limit, including dynamic XLR microphones. The adapter is in an industry standard size.
Cons:
* when closing it up to get some space back the knob of the arm adjustment screw rubbed against the springs which made it rather concerning to fully collapse the unit [-1 star]
* the knurled adapter has thin metal where it connects to the mic mount. This made it extremely difficult to unscrew the shock mount. I had to ultimately use a chamois to grip it, very nearly had to add pliers, additionally. Don’t like that in a piece of studio equipment, even at this price point. [-1 star]
* the mounting clamp only has surface protecting material on the upper side, the static part that touches the top of your desk. The metal screw clamp is just bare metal. I can see it causing some damage if tightened down on the wrong surface. I should deduct an additional star but I won’t, mainly due to the price point.
What I liked:
* the size of the unit. It is perfect for travel, you could definitely fit it into a suitcase for carry on.
* the price. $10 is a fair price but is still a definite selling point for this item
What I didn’t like:
* having to fight to get my mic mount off the unit. Gave me a miniature heart attack because I thought it would be mated with the stand forever.
